newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish oil investor to be asked to develop refiner.
newsitem.headline: Polish oil investor to be asked to develop refiner.

text.p: A prospective foreign investor in one of Poland's two largest oil refineries will be asked to develop a third such facility in the south of country under the oil sector modernisation programme, the government said.

Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said on Monday that a future investor in Petrochemia Plock or Rafineria Gdansk would be required to modernise and boost production at a small refinery in the southern city of Czechowice-Dziedziece.
"The investor in Plock or Gdansk will be expected to provide means for developing Czechowice-Dziedzice," Kaczmarek told a news briefing.
He said that in the first stage of the development the investment should boost the Czechowice-Dziedzice processing capacity to two million tonnes of oil from the current several hundred thousand.
He said investment in Czechowice-Dziedzice was needed to increase Poland's petrol production, which now covers only 80 percent of the domestic consumption.
"Demand for fuels will increase considering the development of our automotive market and the motorway construction programme," Kaczmarek said.

Under the government programme, the state-owned oil holding group Nafta Polska SA is preparing the Plock and Gdansk refineries for sale, with about 30-percent stakes in them due to be offered later this year.
The stake could later be extended to a controlling equity after the buyers fullfil their investment plegdes.
As an incentive, investors in the refineries are to gain access to the lucrative chain of about 1,400 filling stations of state-owned CPN SA company.
CPN shares are to be allocated to Nafta, which has already been given controlling stakes in Plock and Gdansk, but the process is delayed by CPN's trade unions protests.
Poland's oil sector needs about $2.5 billion in investment over the next three years to survive competition of Western firms after a coming lifing of trade barriers protecting the industry.
